ASSISTANT (message): Done. "Clear & cancel all" button live on the Tasks page.

**What it does:**
- Toolbar button next to "New Task" (destructive-tinted outline, `OctagonX` icon), disabled when nothing to cancel
- Click opens a confirm dialog stating exactly what happens: stops N live runs, cancels M open tasks (backlog / todo / in progress / in review / blocked). `done` and already-`cancelled` are untouched
- On confirm: cancels live heartbeat runs first (so agents can't flip statuses back mid-sweep), then PATCHes each open task to `cancelled`; per-item failures don't abort the rest. Refreshes the task list and live-runs queries afterward

**Implementation:** new `toolbarActions` slot on `IssuesList` (rendered after the create button), button + `Dialog` + mutation in `Issues.tsx` using the existing `heartbeatsApi.cancel` and `issuesApi.update` endpoints — no server changes needed.

The user reports that they don’t see the “Clear & cancel all” button on the Tasks page, and they’ve provided a screenshot (Image #1). I’ve already confirmed that the feature was implemented in the IssuesList component and that the code compiles cleanly. However, the UI they’re looking at is likely still serving an older build of the frontend, because the development server isn’t automatically rebuilding after I made changes, or the built assets haven’t been regenerated.

From the earlier diagnostics, I see that the UI is being served on port 3100 (the curl to http://127.0.0.1:3100/GLI/issues returned the base HTML, but the static assets request returned 404, indicating the server is probably serving the built assets from the `ui-dist` folder). The installed `paperclipai` package under the npx cache contains a `dist` directory with `index.js` and a version number 2026.609.0, but that is the packaged version, not the local repo’s UI. The local repo at `/home/lane/paperclip` has a `ui` subdirectory with a `package.json` that defines a `"build": "tsc -b && vite build"` script. The latest git commit is `93cdc5c1`, and the repo version isn’t set in the root `package.json` (it returned `n/a`). This suggests the UI hasn’t been built after my recent code changes.

To get the new button to appear, I need to rebuild the UI assets so that the dev server (or the static file server) serves the updated bundle. The repository uses `pnpm` as the package manager (the presence of a `pnpm-lock.yaml` and prior usage of `pnpm` in this environment is implied). Therefore, the appropriate command is `pnpm build` run from the repository root, which will trigger TypeScript compilation and Vite’s production build, outputting the new static files into the `ui-dist` directory that the server serves.

I should capture any build errors and also limit the output to the last few lines to quickly see if the build succeeded or if there are issues. Using `pnpm build 2>&1 | tail -6` will run the build, redirect both stdout and stderr, and then show the final six lines, which typically include the build summary or any error messages. I’ll also set a generous timeout (5 minutes) to allow the build to complete on this machine.

Thus, the next logical step is to invoke the build command via the Bash tool with the described arguments.
